text:
**For most people, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** The sources broadly agree on this.

## Where LiFePO4 wins
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles to 70-80% capacity. The NMC models in these sources are rated for about 500-1,000 ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). With daily cycling, that's roughly 1.4-2 years for NMC versus 8-11 years for LFP.
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently when they failed (about 259°C vs 731°C peak in one study). LFP isn't fireproof, and one test found it hit thermal runaway sooner under overcharge. Still, milder failures matter for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Cost over time:** One source puts median price at about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is far cheaper.
- **Availability:** Nearly all current mid-size and large stations are LFP. NMC is mostly legacy stock, small compacts, or clearance units.

## Where NMC wins
- **Energy density:** NMC cells hold more energy per pound. In finished stations the gap shrinks a lot, because the inverter, case and fans weigh the same either way. One source found only about a 10% difference. Some LFP units are even lighter per Wh than some NMC ones, so compare the actual spec sheets.

## Caveats
- **Cold weather:** Chemistry matters less than you'd think. Most stations, LFP and NMC alike, won't charge below 32°F. Check your model's manual.
- **Ratings aren't uniform:** Makers rate cycles to 70% or 80% and test under different conditions, so a "4,000 to 70%" claim promises less than "4,000 to 80%".
- **Occasional use:** If you only use it a few times a year for outages, cycle count barely matters, because the battery will age from time first. A working NMC unit doesn't need replacing.

## Bottom line
- **Daily or frequent use, or indoor/vehicle storage:** buy LiFePO4.
- **Light use where weight matters:** either works. Compare specific models and avoid paying LFP prices for an older NMC unit.

**Example LFP pick:** the [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000+ cycle rating to 80%, and a 5-year warranty. It lists at $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF, which the source says it tested in BLUETTI's cart on 2026-10-24. It weighs 24.2 kg (about 53 lb) and isn't expandable, so it suits home backup rather than a system you plan to grow. That link is an affiliate link, and the checkout price is what counts.

Whichever you choose, size the unit to what you need to run before worrying about chemistry.
